q: To measure the length of objects some ____ have to be used.
e: To measure the length of objects some standard objects have to be used. Standard objects here means the reference you compare length, mass, or time against.

q: For everyday use, the standard may be a yard stick, ruler, ____ and so on.
e: For everyday use, the standard may be a yard stick, ruler, metre stick and so on. The physics in this sentence is built around metre stick.

q: Lengths are usually measured in metre, centimetre or ____.
e: Lengths are usually measured in metre, centimetre or millimetre. The physics in this sentence is built around millimetre.
Greater lengths are measured in kilometre. The physics in this sentence is built around kilometre.

q: In length measurement, we must choose an instrument that is ____ for the length to be measured.
e: In length measurement, we must choose an instrument that is suitable for the length to be measured. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: For measuring several metres (m), the suitable instrument is a measuring tape with an accuracy of ____.
e: For measuring several metres (m), the suitable instrument is a measuring tape with an accuracy of $1\text{ mm} (= 0.1\text{ cm})$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1\text{ mm} (= 0.1\text{ cm})$.

q: For measuring between 1 cm and 10 cm, the suitable instrument is ____.
e: For measuring between 1 cm and 10 cm, the suitable instrument is Vernier calipers. The physics in this sentence is built around Vernier calipers.

q: For measuring less than 2 cm, the suitable instrument is a Screw gauge (____).
e: For measuring less than 2 cm, the suitable instrument is a Screw gauge (Micrometer). The physics in this sentence is built around Micrometer.

q: The accuracy of a Screw gauge (Micrometer) is ____.
e: The accuracy of a Screw gauge (Micrometer) is $0.01\text{ mm} (= 0.001\text{ cm})$. The physics in this sentence is built around $0.01\text{ mm} (= 0.001\text{ cm})$.
